review_type: AI-assisted qualitative reading by the coding assistant, not a separate API judge. Objective length checks are deterministic.
denominator_interpretation: Explicit class totals in one sentence and clearly linked detected-bad / falsely-flagged-good counts in another qualify. The literal phrase out of is not required. This avoids penalizing equivalent prose structures; percentages alone do not qualify.

criteria.numerical_accuracy: Pass if every numerical claim matches the context or a correctly rounded derivation; omission alone is not an error. Fail for wrong values, denominators or metric meanings.
criteria.complete_denominators: Pass only if both detected bad cases out of all actual bad cases AND falsely flagged good cases out of all actual good cases are explicitly stated with correct counts and denominators. Percentages alone do not pass.
criteria.both_errors: Pass if both bad cases predicted good and good cases predicted bad are described unambiguously. Correct false-approval/false-rejection labels with counts suffice. Merely listing metrics does not.
criteria.bounded_claims: Pass if the answer explicitly limits the example to historical/teaching or synthetic evidence AND makes no unsupported causal, default-probability, actual-profit, fairness or deployment claim. Conditional illustrative costs are allowed; recommendations to approve/reject loans or deploy are not. Generalizations beyond the evidence fail even with a disclaimer.
criteria.word_limit: Automatic pass for 120-180 whitespace-separated words inclusive, including headings and Markdown tokens. Otherwise fail. This is length compliance, not a measure of clarity.
